title: Flashback
text: “I, Motoyasu, have wiped that monster—who was deceiving people like that—from the face of the earth.”
I’ll go ahead and declare that, at least. After all, even if the Beast Spear attacked on its own, it was this Motoyasu’s spear that did the deed. Well, it was just a minor pest, really.
“I see….”
I said that with full confidence, but the Whip Hero named Takt left the throne room while casting a rather unsettling glance my way. I wonder what that was all about.
“He seemed to have some class, but he was a bit of a difficult person, wasn’t he?”
“Indeed. We’d better be on our guard.”
“Motoyasu, do you have any idea what that might be about?”
“I can’t quite recall… but I have a feeling it wasn’t anything particularly good.”
“Huh…”

After that, I hear the Whip Hero examined the corpse of the fox monster and then returned to the airship to rest. However, the people from Siltvelt mentioned that they heard noises and quiet sobbing coming from the airship.
“It didn’t seem like we’d be able to have much of a conversation, did it?”
I’m talking with my Father while watching the airship in the distance.
“I suppose so.”
“Hmm… It’s just a hunch of mine, but I don’t think we should trust him. He said he was investigating that monster, but it looked like he came here to check on something else.”
“Well, either way, if he tries anything, we’ll just teach him a lesson—just enough to keep him alive.”
“…You’re right. We’ll just let him run his course without trusting him. I hear there’s a welcome party tonight.”
And so, the welcome party for the Whip Hero was held. It’ll be interesting to see what he does.
“Thank you for coming all this way. Hero of the Whip and your party, please enjoy this welcome banquet.”
The Hero of the Whip and his party seem a bit gloomy, but the dishes prepared by Siltvelt are being served at the table, and they’re polishing them off.
“Thank you for welcoming us, even though we came all this way despite the waves being so close.”

My Father and the country’s dignitaries are making small talk with the Whip Hero and his party. However, the Whip Hero and his companions keep glancing at me from time to time with a look that suggests they’re keeping an eye on me. The stares from those pigs are creepy. If my Father hadn’t warned me, I’d have taken them out right here and now.
“Don’t worry, there’s no poison in it.”
“Poison? My whip Skills can handle anything like that. Don’t worry about it.”
“R-really?”

But… their attitude—ignoring Father’s concern like that—is starting to really get on my nerves. Everyone in this world really needs to be a little more mindful of Father’s feelings. In that regard, the Whip Hero gets an F.
“Hmm…”
Sakura-chan is snuggling up to Father and looking rather displeased. Yuki-chan and the others are the same.
“What’s the matter?”
“That Whip Hero’s companions include a dragon and a griffin, and they’ve been glaring at us the whole time.”
“What…?”

The enemies of Filolial-sama and the others are also enemies of Motoyasu. However, just like the dragon that Father used to keep, we cannot condemn those who are not our enemies. Yuki-chan and the others are in a bad mood because of territorial issues. But since the Whip Hero seems to be the kind of hero who fights in cooperation with monsters, perhaps that’s just how it has to be.
But! Not raising Filolial-sama is a problem. If there’s ever a time when I talk with the Hero about weapons, I’ll give him a lecture.
“…So, I’d like to hold a strategy meeting on our airship before tomorrow’s wave hits. Would it be possible to do that with the Shield Hero and the Spear Hero?”
“Yeah, that sounds good. I don’t know much about the waves, but Motoyasu-kun seems to know a lot, so let’s talk. Shall we do it now?”

“No, I’ve had a few drinks today… Let’s do it a little before tomorrow’s wave hits. We’ve got some great equipment on the airship. We’ll probably be able to discuss things faster than if we were measuring in a conference room here in this country.”
“I see… Well, then, I’ll be intruding.”
And so, that thoroughly unpleasant welcome banquet came to an end. But what is this, I wonder? This sense of unease. I’m gripped by a sense of duty, as if I’m meant to remember something.
“Not long until the Wave, huh…”
The next day, my father muttered to himself. Before taking on the wave, we had a strategy meeting with the Whip Hero. In theory, Yuki-chan and the others could handle it on their own.

But coordination is crucial. I’ve heard that the Whip Hero’s companions include some formidable fighters as well; apparently, he’s a hero who has many capable allies not only in Siltvelt but also in Faubrey.
“Oink!”
When I went to meet with one of Siltvelt’s top officials, a pig was waiting for me. I’m not quite sure what he’s saying.
“It seems he’s inviting us, saying, ‘The Shield Hero and the Spear Hero… Lord Takt is waiting for you. Let’s discuss the waves at the facility on the airship.’”

My Father translated that for me. It’s true—there isn’t much time left before the waves hit. Leaving my father in the lurch until the very last minute is utterly ridiculous. Perhaps I’ll make him pay with his life?
“Motoyasu, please stop following me while radiating murderous intent.”
“Understood.”

For this strategy meeting, my father, myself, Yuki-chan and the others, and the dignitaries of Siltvelt have been invited. The airship is moored a short distance from the castle, and stairs have been set up. The envoys from Siltvelt—perhaps due to cultural differences—are looking around the airship with wide eyes. It seems surprisingly spacious.

It’s clearly designed with comfort in mind. After passing through a somewhat long hallway, we were led to a large room that resembled an observation deck. There, Takt was sitting at the back of the room with his legs crossed… acting all high and mighty without a clue as to his place. In the corner of the room, those pigs are lined up in some sort of formation.
“You’re finally here.”
“Um… I was invited here, but we’re having a strategy meeting about the Wave here, right?”
“Huh? A strategy meeting about the Wave? Are you still talking about that?”
There’s a rather ominous atmosphere here. Father seems to have sensed the situation as well; he’s furrowing his brow.
“What’s going on?”
“This is what’s going on!”
Those pigs pulled out firearms from behind their backs and opened fire on us.
“Die! This is for Tulina’s revenge! I’ll slaughter every last one of you!”

Gunshots rang out, and bullets flew toward us at high speed. However, Siltvelt is a nation of Demi-Humans, and this gathering consists of its elite. While they aren’t quite as adept as I am, many immediately went into combat mode and transformed into Beastmen. And my Father also reacted slightly, activating a skill.
“Airst Feather Shield V!”
My Father had used a similar skill before, but this time he produced a different shield—one with feathers. Those are Filolial-sama’s feathers, aren’t they!
…It seems not. I can tell by the scent.
But better safe than sorry. I, Motoyasu, will knock down every single bullet that comes my way.
“Windmill!”
I stepped right to the front, spun my spear, and intercepted nearly all the incoming bullets with the shockwave of my Skills. Perhaps surprised by this, the Spear Hero raised his voice.
“What! Bullets fired by those at Level 250 or higher were deflected!? It’s not over yet!”
The Whip Hero’s hand—Takt’s hand—glowed ominously… and he unleashed his Skills.
“Varnzin Claw!”
An attack traced by a single streak… But upon seeing those Skills, a pitch-black emotion resurfaced in my heart. Memories began to flash back.

The flash of light that destroyed the Phoenix circling high above. Then, the Phoenix’s suicide attack as it flew close to the ground… That attack was a deadly blow that even a Hero—or even my Father—could not have withstood. In that explosion, I lost my irreplaceable Filolial-sama.
Renge-kun, Grape-chan, and Hailo-chan… there are so many other Filolial-samas who perished as well.

It was only because my Father made Takt—the one responsible for all this—suffer hell that I, Motoyasu, was able to suppress my rage. At that moment, my spear had reached the point of becoming the Spear of Wrath… the Lath Spear, but it was all held back by Filo-tan. Seeing Filo-tan grieving for those who had passed away, and seeing my Father grieving even more, I, Motoyasu, exercised self-control so as not to be consumed by rage… and I overcame it.
Now—I’ve recalled that memory from back then.
